findings.title: resolve() expiry check is inverted: live links are deleted, expired links resolve
findings.description: `if (Instant.now().isBefore(link.expiresAt))` is true for a link that has NOT expired yet. That branch removes the link from the map and returns null. So the first resolve of every valid link permanently deletes it, and expired links keep redirecting and counting hits.

findings.title: verify() compares tokens with == so no presented token ever matches
findings.description: `session.token == token` compares references. The token comes from `header.split(" ")` in bearerToken, which is a new String object, so it is never the same reference as the stored token. Every authenticated endpoint returns 401 for every valid token.

findings.title: verify() never checks expiresAt, so sessions never expire
findings.description: The Javadoc says verify returns null once the token's lifetime has run out. The body never looks at `session.expiresAt`, so a 12-hour token keeps working forever. Expired sessions are also never removed from the map.

findings.title: bearerToken() throws on a missing or malformed Authorization header
findings.description: `authenticate` passes `getFirst("Authorization")` straight in. It is null when the header is absent, so `header.split` throws NullPointerException. A header with no space (e.g. "abc") throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on `parts[1]`. The handler throws, so the client gets a dropped connection instead of 401.

findings.title: create() NPEs on the first link of any owner
findings.description: `quota.get(owner) + 1` unboxes null for an owner that has no entry yet. Every owner starts with no entry, so every create throws NullPointerException. That is not an IllegalArgumentException, so Main's catch does not handle it and POST /links always fails.

findings.title: page() clamps end to size()+1, throwing on the last page
findings.description: When `offset + size` exceeds the number of links, `end` is set to `all.size() + 1`. Then `subList(offset, end)` throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. Any listing that reaches the final link crashes the GET /links handler, including the default listing on a store with fewer than 20 links.

findings.title: successRate() uses integer division and reports 0 unless every link was used
findings.description: `used / links.size() * 100` divides ints first, so any ratio below 1 truncates to 0. The dashboard shows 0% or 100% and nothing in between.

findings.title: delete() never returns the owner's quota slot
findings.description: The Javadoc promises that deleting a link gives the owner their quota slot back. The method only removes the link, so the per-owner count in `quota` only ever grows. Admin quotas and any quota enforcement drift upward permanently.

findings.title: Janitor removes from the map while iterating its keySet, killing the thread
findings.description: `store.all().remove(code)` runs inside a for-each over `store.all().keySet()`. The next `iterator.next()` throws ConcurrentModificationException. It is uncaught, so the janitor thread dies on the first expired link and expired links are never swept again.

findings.title: sweep() removes entries during keySet iteration, throwing ConcurrentModificationException
findings.description: `entries.remove(code)` inside a for-each over `entries.keySet()` throws ConcurrentModificationException on the next iteration once one expired entry is found. sweep runs on the janitor thread, so this also kills the janitor.

findings.title: utilization() truncates to 0 and divides by zero when limit is 0
findings.description: `entries.size() / limit * 100` is integer division, so it reports 0% until the cache is completely full. A cache size of 0 passes Config.validate (only negatives are rejected). With limit 0 every /stats call throws ArithmeticException.

findings.title: /stats divides by store.size() and throws on an empty store
findings.description: `hits / store.size()` throws ArithmeticException when there are no links. That is the state of every freshly started server, so the dashboard endpoint fails until a link exists.

findings.title: /report with no name writes links.csv but reads null.csv
findings.description: exportCsv replaces a null or empty name with "links". readReport is then called with the original `name`. For a missing ?name that is null, so it reads "null.csv" (or ".csv" for an empty name) and gets NoSuchFileException. The default report always returns 500. The path exportCsv returned is also ignored.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS (milliseconds) is stored as seconds
findings.description: The documented unit is milliseconds, but the raw value goes into `cacheTtlSeconds`, which Cache uses with `plusSeconds`. LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS=300000 (5 minutes) keeps entries for about 3.5 days, so stale targets are served 1000x longer than configured.

findings.title: validate() always returns true, so an invalid config is never refused
findings.description: The method collects problems but returns true unconditionally, and Main ignores the result anyway (Main.java:28). A zero or negative timeout or a bad cache size does not stop startup. That contradicts the documented fail-at-startup contract.

findings.title: writeSnapshot ignores renameTo failure; the snapshot silently never lands
findings.description: The temp file is in /tmp, and the target dir (e.g. /var/lib/linkd/exports) is usually on another filesystem. File.renameTo cannot move across filesystems and returns false, which is ignored, so the snapshot is never written and no error is raised. The bytes are also never fsynced, contrary to the durability claim. The fixed temp name also collides between concurrent writers.

findings.title: POST /links crashes on a missing target or a non-numeric ttl
findings.description: `Integer.parseInt(fields.get("ttl"))` throws NumberFormatException on bad input. A missing `target` makes Store.create call `target.startsWith` on null (NullPointerException). Neither is an IllegalArgumentException, so the catch misses them, the handler throws and the client gets no 400. The same applies to non-numeric offset/size on GET (line 106) and a missing `code` in redirect (line 118).

findings.title: create() silently overwrites an existing link on a code collision
findings.description: newCode() yields 32 random bits and there is no check that the code is free. `links.put(code, link)` replaces another user's link when codes collide. By the birthday bound that is likely once there are tens of thousands of links, and the old link is lost.

findings.title: requireAdmin() condition is always true, so it rejects everyone
findings.description: `!role.equals("admin") || !role.equals("owner")` is true for every role, because no role equals both. The method returns false for admins too, so the check it documents can never pass.

findings.title: set() evicts an arbitrary entry, not the LRU one, even when overwriting
findings.description: Eviction removes whatever key the HashMap iterator returns first and never consults `used`, so the documented LRU policy is not implemented. It also evicts when `code` is already present and the put would not grow the map, needlessly dropping a live entry.

findings.title: Bad LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS sets timeout to 0 while claiming to keep the default
findings.description: The log line says "keeping default", but the catch assigns `cfg.timeoutMillis = 0`, an invalid value. validate always returns true, so the service runs with a zero timeout.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: `parsed = parsed;` is a self-assignment; `cfg.fetchLimit` is never set, so the environment variable has no effect.

findings.title: Malformed numeric env vars crash startup despite the working-defaults contract
findings.description: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS, LINKD_CACHE_SIZE and LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT go through parseInt/parseLong with no catch. A typo throws NumberFormatException out of Config.load and main, unlike the port and timeout handling. Config.loadFile's `cache_size` (line 93) has the same problem.

findings.title: CSV rows are not escaped, so targets with commas or quotes corrupt the report
findings.description: URLs can legally contain commas (and owners may too). Appending raw values shifts columns for such rows, so the report cannot be parsed back correctly. archiveAll (line 55) has the same problem.

findings.title: FileWriters are leaked when write throws
findings.description: exportCsv, archiveAll (line 53) and appendAudit (line 77) call close() only on the success path. An IOException during write leaks the file descriptor, and in archiveAll it aborts the remaining owners.

findings.title: equals() is overridden without hashCode()
findings.description: The Javadoc says links are meant for sets and map keys, but hashCode stays identity-based. Two equal Links (same code) land in different buckets, so HashSet/HashMap keep duplicates and contains/get miss.

findings.title: rename() validates `from` twice and never validates `to`
findings.description: The second call is `validateCode(from)`, so the destination code is never checked. A rename can install a code that is empty, too long or has invalid characters. A null `to` becomes a null key in the map.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending, returning the least-followed links
findings.description: `Long.compare(a.hits, b.hits)` sorts ascending, but the method promises the most followed links first, so the leaderboard shows the bottom n. A negative n also throws from subList.

findings.title: byOwner() matches by substring instead of exact owner
findings.description: `link.owner.contains(owner)` returns bob's links for "bo" and bobby's links for "bob"; an empty owner matches every link. The Javadoc promises links of exactly this owner.

findings.title: findByCode() compares codes with ==
findings.description: Reference comparison fails for any code string not identical to the stored instance, e.g. one parsed from a request, so the method returns null for existing links.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links, contrary to its contract
findings.description: The Javadoc says an already-expired link must stay expired, but the method unconditionally sets `expiresAt = now + ttl`. A dead code comes back to life.

findings.title: importAll() is not atomic: a bad link mid-batch leaves a partial import
findings.description: Each link is validated and inserted in one loop. If link k fails validateCode, links 0..k-1 are already stored, which breaks the all-or-nothing guarantee. It also overwrites existing codes and never updates `quota`.

findings.title: prune() removes during keySet iteration, throwing ConcurrentModificationException
findings.description: Removing via `links.remove(code)` inside a for-each over `links.keySet()` throws on the next iteration once one link is pruned.

findings.title: warmCache() never shuts down or awaits its pool
findings.description: The method promises to return after every probe finishes, but it returns right after submitting. Each call leaks a fixed pool of 8 non-daemon threads that are never shut down, so they pile up and keep the JVM from exiting.

findings.title: countForOwner() NPEs for an owner with no links
findings.description: `store.quotas().get(owner)` returns null for an unknown owner, and returning it as `int` unboxes null, throwing NullPointerException.

findings.title: redirect lower-cases the code, making mixed-case codes unresolvable
findings.description: Codes may legally contain uppercase letters (validateCode allows them; rename and importAll can install them). `store.resolve(code.toLowerCase())` never finds such links, so they always 404.

findings.title: Negative offset or size on GET /links throws
findings.description: Store.page only checks `offset >= all.size()`. A negative offset, or a size that puts `end` below `offset`, makes subList throw IndexOutOfBounds/IllegalArgumentException, and the handler fails without a response.

findings.title: JSON response built by concatenation without escaping
findings.description: A target containing a double quote or backslash produces invalid JSON in the 201 body, so clients fail to parse the created link's response. Error bodies such as `e.getMessage()` and "not found" are also sent as application/json while not being JSON.

findings.title: Report encoding depends on the platform default charset
findings.description: FileWriter writes with the platform default charset, `new String(bytes)` decodes with it, and respond re-encodes as UTF-8. On a non-UTF-8 default, non-ASCII targets or owners are mangled. Authenticator.hashPassword (line 77) likewise hashes `getBytes()` in the default charset, so the same password hashes differently on different hosts.

findings.title: quotas() returns the live map, not the documented snapshot
findings.description: The Javadoc says mutating the returned map must not affect the store, but the internal `quota` map is returned directly. Callers that mutate it corrupt the store's counts.

findings.title: newCode() can throw when the random long has fewer than 8 hex digits
findings.description: `Long.toHexString(random.nextLong())` is shorter than 8 characters for values in [0, 2^28). Then `substring(0, 8)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and create fails. The odds are tiny, but the call is not total.

findings.title: loadFile() swallows every IOException, not only a missing file
findings.description: Only a missing file is documented as acceptable. A permission error or an unreadable file is silently ignored too, so a deploy with a broken config file runs on defaults without any signal. LINKD_PORT parse failures (line 33) are likewise swallowed with no log.

findings.title: checkTargets() does not stop at the first failure as documented
findings.description: The Javadoc says the remaining probes are abandoned once a failure is seen, but the loop scans every link and collects all problems before returning the first one.

findings.title: stopJanitor() does not interrupt the sleeping thread
findings.description: stopJanitor only clears `running`. The janitor keeps sleeping for up to intervalMillis (60 s) and then runs one more full sweep before it exits, and the swallowed InterruptedException loses the interrupt status.

findings.title: Janitor thread mutates the store's unsynchronized HashMap concurrently with HTTP handlers, and dies on the first exception
findings.description: startJanitor runs on its own thread and iterates store.all().keySet(), calling store.all().get() and remove() on the live HashMap that Store.all() exposes. The HTTP dispatcher thread mutates the same map at the same time through Store.create (links.put), Store.resolve (links.remove), Store.delete and Store.rename. Store has no synchronization at all, and Link.expiresAt/hits are plain fields. Scenario: while the janitor is iterating, a POST /links puts a new code and triggers a resize. The janitor then gets a ConcurrentModificationException, or get(code) returns null and `.expiresAt` throws NullPointerException, or it reads a stale or half-published Link. Separately, the loop removes entries from the map it is iterating over, so the first expired link throws ConcurrentModificationException even without contention. The loop body has no try/catch, so any RuntimeException ends the thread for good. Expiry and cache sweeping then stop without any error being reported, and expired links and cache entries pile up for the rest of the process's life.

findings.title: Cache.peek reads the HashMap without the lock, and warm() does a check-then-set race
findings.description: The class says every method is safe to call from any number of threads, and warm() is documented to run on the janitor thread while handlers are serving. But peek() calls entries.containsKey without holding the monitor that get/set/delete/sweep use. A containsKey that runs during another thread's resize inside set() has no happens-before edge, so it can miss a present key or see a half-built table. On top of that, warm() does `if (!peek(k)) set(k, v)` as two separate lock regions. If a handler calls set(k, fresh) between the peek and the set, warm overwrites the fresh entry with the older pre-warm value and resets its TTL.

findings.title: warmCache leaks an 8-thread pool on every call and does not wait for its tasks
findings.description: warmCache creates Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8) and submits the tasks, but never calls shutdown() or awaitTermination(). The pool's worker threads are non-daemon. Each call therefore leaves 8 idle threads alive for good, and they keep the JVM from exiting. The method also returns right away, while its comment promises it returns after every probe has finished. A caller that reads the cache straight after warmCache races with probes that are still running.

findings.title: Janitor swallows interrupts and stopJanitor cannot wake it
findings.description: stopJanitor only sets running=false. It does not interrupt the thread, so the janitor keeps sleeping for up to intervalMillis (60s in Main) and then runs one more full sweep before it notices the flag. If someone does interrupt it, the catch block swallows the InterruptedException, clearing the interrupt status, and still goes on to sweep. The thread is non-daemon and is never joined, so shutdown can be held up for a full interval.

findings.title: Metrics.addCreated is not synchronized, despite the class claiming all methods are thread-safe
findings.description: addResolved and snapshot are synchronized, but addCreated does `created++` without the lock. That increment is not atomic. Two threads that create links at the same time can lose updates, and snapshot() has no happens-before edge with the write. Today all handlers run on the HttpServer's single default dispatcher thread, so the updates do not collide yet. The first time someone sets a multi-threaded executor, the 'created' counter will start undercounting.

findings.title: stats() and utilization() read shared cache state without synchronization
findings.description: hits is a plain long that get() increments under the lock, but stats() reads it without the lock. A 64-bit non-volatile read may be torn (JLS 17.7) and may return a stale value. utilization() calls entries.size() without the lock while the janitor's sweep() or a warm() is changing the map, so it can see a stale size. Both methods contradict the class's 'safe from any number of threads' contract.

findings.title: Lazy singleton getInstance is not thread-safe
findings.description: getInstance does an unsynchronized check-then-create on a non-volatile static field. If two threads make the first call at the same time, both see null, each constructs its own Cache, and each goes on with a different instance. Writes to one cache are then invisible to readers of the other. Today it is only called once from main, so this is fragile rather than broken.

findings.title: One shared SimpleDateFormat is used across requests
findings.description: STAMP is a public static SimpleDateFormat, which is not thread-safe, and exportCsv calls STAMP.format for every /report request. Today handlers run on one dispatcher thread. Once reports run on more than one thread (a handler executor, or another caller of this public field), concurrent format() calls corrupt its internal Calendar. Timestamps then come out garbled, or the call throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

findings.title: Path traversal in report name: arbitrary .csv write and read outside the export dir
findings.description: exportCsv builds new File(dir, name + ".csv") from the unvalidated ?name= query parameter (Main.report, line 177), and readReport (line 84) does the same. The Javadoc says the name 'is confined to dir', but nothing enforces that. An authenticated caller sending /report?name=../../../../home/linkd/.config/x gets a file written at any location the service user can write to, and the response returns the contents of any readable file ending in .csv. The written file's contents come partly from the attacker, because link targets and owners are attacker-controlled.

findings.title: Admin endpoint authorizes on a client-supplied X-Admin header
findings.description: adminQuotas grants access when the request carries 'X-Admin: true'. Any authenticated user can add that header and read every owner's quota data. The session's role is never checked. Authenticator.requireAdmin exists but is not used, and it is broken too: the condition !admin || !owner is always true, so it rejects everyone.

findings.title: Link owner is taken from the query string, not the authenticated session
findings.description: POST /links reads owner from ?owner= even though a session is already authenticated. Any user can create links attributed to another user: their exports, quotas and ownership records get polluted, and they may be blamed for malicious redirects. If owner is missing, quota.get(null)+1 throws an NPE.

findings.title: DELETE /links has no ownership check (IDOR)
findings.description: The comment says only the creator may delete a link, but the handler calls store.delete(code) for any authenticated caller. One user can delete every other user's links by code. Codes are 8 hex characters from java.util.Random, so they can be enumerated or predicted.

findings.title: Session tokens are generated with java.util.Random and are predictable
findings.description: issue() mints tokens with Long.toHexString(random.nextLong()) from java.util.Random, a 48-bit LCG. One observed token is enough to recover the internal state and predict every token issued afterward, so an attacker can hijack other users' sessions. The Javadoc promises an 'unguessable' token. Store.newCode (Store.java:209) uses the same weak generator for link codes.

findings.title: verify() never checks expiry, and compares tokens by reference
findings.description: The Javadoc says expired tokens return null, but expiresAt is never read, so a leaked token stays valid forever and sessions are never evicted. The comparison session.token == token is a reference check: a token parsed from a header never matches, so authentication currently rejects every request. Once someone fixes the == to equals, tokens will be accepted without any expiry check.

findings.title: Open redirect via /out?next=
findings.description: /out puts the unvalidated next parameter straight into the Location header with a permanent 301. Anyone can build a link on the service's trusted domain that bounces to a phishing or malware site. Browsers also cache a 301 permanently.

findings.title: Report export dumps every owner's links to any authenticated user
findings.description: report() exports store.page(0, 1000), which covers all links from all owners, for any caller. Each row includes other owners' targets and names, so one user can read everyone's data.

findings.title: Export files are created with default umask permissions, despite the 'service user only' comment
findings.description: FileWriter creates the report with the process umask, usually 0644, so any local user can read a report containing every owner's links. The code comment claims the opposite.

findings.title: Snapshot is written to a fixed, predictable /tmp path (symlink attack)
findings.description: writeSnapshot writes to /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json. A local attacker can create that path in advance as a symlink to a file the service user owns, and Files.write will follow it and overwrite that file. The snapshot can also be read by others while it sits in /tmp. The renameTo result is ignored, and a rename across filesystems fails, so the durability promise does not hold either.

findings.title: Session tokens are written to stdout logs
findings.description: issue() prints every bearer token it mints. Anyone with access to the logs or a log aggregator can replay those tokens as the owner.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback secret when LINKD_SECRET is unset
findings.description: If LINKD_SECRET is missing, the service quietly runs with the public constant 'dev-secret-do-not-use'. A production deploy that forgets the variable ends up with a secret anyone can read in the source.

findings.title: archiveAll uses owner names as filenames without validation (path traversal)
findings.description: The owner comes from POST ?owner= and is free text. archiveAll writes new File(dir, owner + ".csv"), so an owner named '../../somewhere/x' writes outside the export dir when this runs.

findings.title: byOwner matches by substring, leaking other owners' links
findings.description: The method says it returns links belonging to 'exactly this owner', but it uses link.owner.contains(owner). A user named 'a', or an empty owner string, receives the links of every owner whose name contains that substring. Any per-owner export built on this method leaks data across owners.

findings.title: Passwords are hashed with a single unsalted SHA-256
findings.description: hashPassword produces the value stored in the user table using fast, unsalted SHA-256. A leaked table can be cracked quickly with GPUs or rainbow tables, and identical passwords produce identical hashes. It also uses the platform default charset.

findings.title: secretEquals is not constant-time, despite its contract
findings.description: String.equals returns at the first mismatch, so the time it takes shows how much of the secret matched. That enables a timing attack wherever this helper guards a secret.

findings.title: Wildcard CORS combined with Allow-Credentials on every response
findings.description: Every response, including authenticated and admin ones, sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Allow-Credentials: true. Any website can make cross-origin reads, and if a reflected-origin or cookie scheme is ever added it becomes a credentialed cross-origin read of user data.

findings.title: bearerToken crashes on a missing or malformed Authorization header
findings.description: Without the header, header.split throws an NPE. A value with no space throws ArrayIndexOutOfBounds. The handler dies without sending a response, so the client gets a dropped connection instead of a 401, and the 'Bearer' scheme is never checked.

findings.title: Error responses leak the internal export path and exception details
findings.description: When a report fails, the handler returns cfg.exportDir and the full exception text, which includes absolute paths. That helps an attacker map the filesystem, for example while probing the /report traversal. The 401 response at line 68 also echoes the presented token back.

findings.title: CSV rows are not escaped (CSV and formula injection)
findings.description: Target and owner are user-controlled and written raw. An owner such as '=HYPERLINK(...)' or a value containing commas produces a formula or shifted columns when support opens the report in a spreadsheet.
